text:
## Observations

1. When a new position is added, each old non-empty subsequence appears both unchanged and extended by the new element. The new singleton has score zero.
2. Exactly \(2^{i-1}\) subsequences end at position \(i\), because each earlier position can be chosen independently.
3. The identity \(\gcd(x,y)=\sum_{d\mid x,\ d\mid y}\varphi(d)\) turns each GCD contribution into a sum over common divisors, where \(\varphi\) is Euler’s totient function.
4. Every divisor needed is at most \(M=\max_i A_i\), and enumerating the multiples of each \(d\le M\) visits every divisor entry once.
5. All updates use only addition and multiplication, so totals and powers of two can be maintained modulo \(998244353\).

## Solution sketch

1. > Every divisor needed is at most \(M=\max_i A_i\), and enumerating the multiples of each \(d\le M\) visits every divisor entry once.

   Read the input and compute \(M\). Precompute the divisor lists by appending each \(d\) to the list of every multiple of \(d\). Compute the totients with a sieve. Initialize \(\varphi(x)=x\), then subtract \(\varphi(x)/p\) using integer division for each prime \(p\) and each multiple \(x\) of \(p\). This gives \(\varphi(1)=1\).

2. > Exactly \(2^{i-1}\) subsequences end at position \(i\), because each earlier position can be chosen independently.

   Initialize an array \(W\) to zero. Before processing position \(m\), \(W[d]\) represents the number of subsequences of the previous prefix whose final value is divisible by \(d\). After using the old counts at position \(m\), add \(2^{m-1}\) to \(W[d]\) for every divisor \(d\) of \(A_m\). Equal values at different positions contribute separately.

3. > The identity \(\gcd(x,y)=\sum_{d\mid x,\ d\mid y}\varphi(d)\) turns each GCD contribution into a sum over common divisors, where \(\varphi\) is Euler’s totient function.

   At position \(m\), compute the total contribution of the newly formed adjacent pairs as \(C=\sum_{d\mid A_m}\varphi(d)W[d]\). In one pass over the divisors of \(A_m\), use each old \(W[d]\) in the sum before applying that entry’s update from step 2.

4. > When a new position is added, each old non-empty subsequence appears both unchanged and extended by the new element. The new singleton has score zero.

   Start with a prefix total of zero. At each position, double the previous total and add \(C\), then output the result modulo \(998244353\). At the first position, all old counts are zero, so the first output is zero, including when \(N=1\). If \(A_m=1\), its divisor list contains only \(1\), which correctly adds one for each extension of an old non-empty subsequence.

5. > All updates use only addition and multiplication, so totals and powers of two can be maintained modulo \(998244353\).

   Keep the entries of \(W\), the prefix total, and the current power of two reduced modulo \(998244353\). Start the power at \(1\) and double it modulo \(998244353\) after each position. Precomputation takes \(O(M\log(M+1))\) time and space. The scan takes \(O\bigl(N+\sum_{m=1}^{N}\tau(A_m)\bigr)\) time, where \(\tau(x)\) counts the divisors of \(x\). Including the input and buffered output, total space is \(O(N+M\log(M+1))\).

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
